# Input method comparison

An input method passes only when real non-Latin text reaches a real application. Advertising `text-input-v3` or `input-method-v2` is not an input path; it is a promise that one could exist. Japanese, Chinese and Korean are tested separately because they fail separately, and candidate-popup positioning is tested because an IME whose candidate window lands in the wrong place is unusable even when the text arrives.

| Gate | Mandatory | Smithay | libmutter |
|---|---|---|---|
| input-method-v2 or equivalent working input path | **yes** | `NOT_RUN` | `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` |
| IBus or Fcitx 5 | no | `NOT_RUN` | `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` |
| English input | no | `NOT_RUN` | `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` |
| Japanese input | no | `NOT_RUN` | `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` |
| Chinese input | no | `NOT_RUN` | `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` |
| Korean input where available | no | `NOT_RUN` | `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` |
| candidate-popup positioning | no | `NOT_RUN` | `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` |
| on-screen-keyboard path | no | `NOT_RUN` | `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` |

Recorded reasons:

- compositor/bunny-mutter-v4 has no downstream shell implementation yet, so there is nothing to measure.
- not executed in V4. The V3 prototype is the starting point; no V4 measurement has been made.

## Status

No gate in this matrix has been measured. Nothing here supports a framework selection, and nothing here may be cited as qualification evidence.
